I don't really know why I'm writing this. Maybe I'm just tired, or maybe I've been tired for so long that I don't remember what feeling normal is supposed to be like anymore. The weird part is that nothing particularly bad happened today. I woke up, went to school, talked to people, laughed at some stupid jokes, ate lunch, and came home. Just another normal day. If someone asked me how everything went, I'd probably say it was fine, because technically it was. That's what makes this so frustrating. How do you explain feeling terrible when you can't even point to something terrible happening?

Sometimes I feel like I'm watching everyone else move forward while I'm just pretending to keep up. My classmates talk about their plans, their relationships, their achievements, and all the things they're excited about. I smile and listen because I genuinely want them to be happy. But there's this uncomfortable feeling I can't explain. It's not exactly jealousy. I don't want their lives. I just wish I could look at my own and feel the same excitement they seem to have.

And I know people care about me. At least, I think they do. My friends message me, my family asks whether I've eaten, and people notice when I'm absent. So I feel stupid whenever I start thinking that nobody really knows me. It's unfair to them because they haven't necessarily done anything wrong. They're good people. Maybe I'm just expecting them to understand something I haven't even figured out myself.

The other day, I was sitting with my friends, and everyone was laughing about something. I laughed too, and for a few seconds, I actually felt happy. Then suddenly I became aware of how hard I was trying to stay involved in the conversation. I started wondering whether I would've been missed if I hadn't been sitting there. Not in some dramatic way. Just whether the conversation would've continued exactly the same. It probably would have, which is normal.
